strengths: Strong empirical motivation with compelling analysis of scale and spatial redundancy in VAR (Figures 2-3)
Substantial practical efficiency gains: 3.0-4.2× GPU memory reduction without sacrificing performance
Comprehensive experimental validation including thorough ablation studies and comparisons across multiple baseline categories
Technically sound implementation with clear mathematical formulation and good presentation
Competitive or superior quantitative results (FID 3.09 vs 3.55 for VAR-310M; IS 285.5 vs 280.4)
weaknesses: Limited novelty: scale-Markov conditioning and spatial-Markov attention are straightforward applications of existing concepts (local window attention is well-established)

Narrow evaluation scope: only ImageNet 256×256 evaluation; no results at higher resolutions (512×512, 1024×1024) or other datasets; missing comparisons with other VAR efficiency methods (FastVAR, Infinity)
Weak theoretical justification for Markovian assumptions: no principled analysis of approximation error or formal characterization of information loss from discarding non-adjacent scales
Fine-tuning results conflate multiple factors: unclear whether improvements come from Markovian conditioning, fine-tuning itself, or different computational allocation
Incomplete complexity analysis: asymptotic O(Nk) doesn't account for constant factors; training speedups not clearly demonstrated; wall-clock time comparisons limited
Missing statistical rigor: no error bars, confidence intervals, or multiple runs; unclear if improvements are statistically significant
Hyperparameter sensitivity: neighborhood size k requires careful tuning with substantial FID variation (Table 4: 4.18-4.36)
Ad-hoc design choices: causal mask behavior differs between scales (Figure 7) without clear justification; diagonal pattern masking for r1-r8 appears unmotivated

strengths: Well-motivated empirical analysis: Figures 2-3 convincingly demonstrate scale and spatial redundancy in VAR through attention weight visualizations and attention maps
Significant practical impact: 3-4× memory reduction (4.2× at inference) and complete elimination of KV cache, enabling training on modest hardware (8 RTX 4090 GPUs)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Multiple model sizes (310M-1B), detailed ablations on key components, multiple metrics, and pre-trained/fine-tuning comparisons showing consistent improvements
Strong computational complexity reduction: From O(N²) to O(N·k) with clear mathematical derivation and detailed complexity analysis in appendix
Technically sound methodology: Clean mathematical formulation (Eqs. 4-7), clever diagonal causal mask strategy for parallel training, and thorough implementation documentation
Thorough ablation studies: Systematic analysis of conditioning prefix length, neighborhood size k, and ablations on individual components with clear progression
Clear presentation and reproducibility: Well-structured paper with effective visualizations, detailed hyperparameters (Table 5), and good implementation details
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: Markovian assumptions and neighborhood attention are well-established techniques; the contribution is primarily engineering-focused optimization of VAR rather than introducing new modeling principles

Weak theoretical justification for scale-Markovian assumption: Attention weight distributions do not rigorously prove conditional independence; information could still flow through other mechanisms even with low attention weights, and no analysis of actual modeling capacity loss
Modest performance improvements: FID gains are marginal (3.09 vs 3.55 on 310M, 2.23 vs 2.33 on 1B), with larger models showing negligible improvements; no statistical significance testing provided

Asymmetric and unjustified training procedure: Scales r9-r10 (60% of tokens) revert to single-scale conditioning without causal masking, contradicting the claimed uniform scale-Markovian approach; this design choice lacks explanation

Limited experimental scope: Only ImageNet 256×256 evaluated; no higher-resolution experiments where efficiency matters most; only class-conditional generation tested; missing comparisons with concurrent efficiency methods (HART, FastVAR, collaborative decoding)

Fixed hyperparameter choices lack generalization analysis: k=7×7 neighborhood chosen empirically but not validated to generalize across resolutions or other domains; k is relatively large (49 tokens) limiting complexity savings

Incomplete analysis of discrepancies: Table 2 shows decreased Recall in some cases; Table 3 shows non-linear scaling behavior with single-scale conditioning (FID 4.35 on 310M vs 2.23 on 1B) that isn't explained
Unanswered generalization questions: No evidence that Markovian assumptions hold for higher resolutions, text-to-image synthesis, or other conditioning modalities; limited to single benchmark

strengths: Well-motivated empirical observations: Figures 2-3 convincingly demonstrate scale and spatial redundancy in vanilla next-scale prediction through attention weight analysis
Significant practical improvements: 3-4× memory reduction during both training and inference, enabling training on 8 RTX 4090 GPUs instead of requiring substantially larger resources
Comprehensive experimental validation: Multiple datasets (ImageNet, CelebA, FFHQ), resolutions (256×512), model sizes (310M-2B), with thorough ablations examining each component's contribution
Clear presentation and visualization: Figures effectively communicate conceptual differences; paper is well-written and easy to follow
Solid empirical results: MVAR achieves comparable or superior generation quality (e.g., FID 3.09 vs 3.55 for VAR-d16) while substantially reducing memory footprint
Good reproducibility: Detailed implementation details, hyperparameter settings in appendices, commitment to release code
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: Scale-Markov conditioning is a straightforward simplification rather than a novel principle; spatial-Markov attention is well-established (Hassani & Shi 2022) with main contribution being application to VAR rather than methodological advance

Insufficient justification of Markovian assumptions: Attention weight analysis shows concentration on adjacent structures but doesn't prove information from non-adjacent scales is unnecessary; no quantitative analysis of information loss; improvements could stem from regularization rather than removing true redundancy

Marginal quality improvements lack statistical rigor: FID improvements range from 0.08-0.46 depending on model; IS improvements 1-5%; no statistical significance testing or error bars; improvements could be within noise margins

Unfair experimental comparisons: Section D.1 acknowledges inability to replicate original VAR settings; Table 2 uses different batch sizes and schedules; VAR-d24 hits OOM making direct comparison impossible; confounding factors obscure whether improvements are from method or implementation

Complex mixed training strategy: Parallel training for r1-r8 with custom CUDA kernels for r9-r10 adds implementation complexity; Figure 9 shows concatenated training also works, questioning necessity of mixed approach

Missing critical ablations and comparisons: No comparison with other VAR efficiency methods (FastVAR mentioned but not compared); no ablation training VAR with identical Markovian constraints to isolate MVAR's unique contribution from regularization effects

Hyperparameter selection lacks principled guidance: Neighborhood size k requires empirical tuning with no theoretical justification; unclear how to select k for new resolutions or domains; Table 9 shows performance is stable but still requires tuning

Limited theoretical analysis and generalization: No formal analysis of approximation quality or information-theoretic bounds; all experiments on resolutions ≤512×512; unclear if assumptions hold at higher resolutions; limited exploration beyond natural images

Insufficient analysis of why removing dependencies improves performance: Paper shows MVAR works but doesn't explain why discarding non-adjacent scale connections sometimes improves over baseline; unclear if information is truly redundant

Modest gains relative to complexity: While memory efficiency is significant, generation quality improvements are small and require complex training procedures, limiting impact for scenarios where memory is not the bottleneck
